_note: MITRE ATT&CK reference for the techniques validated in this lab (= the LAB_TECHNIQUES enum in e2e_soc_orchestrator.py). Used by the agent's get_mitre_context() tool and doubles as the E-1 catalog source. Descriptions condensed from ATT&CK v15. Enriched 2026-08-21 with reference links, tools actually observed in THIS lab, and known-false-positive notes discovered live during the 2026-08-20 attack campaign.

T1190.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
T1190.desc: Adversary exploits a weakness in an internet-facing host/app (e.g. SQL injection, RCE) to gain initial access. In this lab: the Juice Shop DMZ app.
T1190.detection: Web Application Attack signatures on the DMZ path; SQLi/XSS/LFI ElastAlert rules.

T1046.name: Network Service Discovery
T1046.desc: Adversary enumerates services/ports to find exploitable targets. In this lab: nmap from Kali.
T1046.detection: ET SCAN Nmap NSE User-Agent; pfsense_portscan cardinality rule (blind to Tailscale-sourced scans, see E-3).
T1046.note: GreyNoise (added by Badr) can distinguish mass internet-background scanning from a targeted probe against us specifically — use run_analyzer for genuinely ambiguous external recon.

T1003.002.name: OS Credential Dumping: Security Account Manager
T1003.002.desc: Dumping the Windows SAM database to extract password hashes, e.g. reg save HKLM\SAM.
T1003.002.detection: Sysmon process-create on reg.exe saving HKLM\SAM or HKLM\SYSTEM.

T1110.name: Brute Force
T1110.desc: Repeated credential-guessing against an authentication service (SMB, SSH, web login).
T1110.detection: Windows Logon Brute-Force rule; linux_ssh_bruteforce (can be starved by host-level fail2ban, confirmed live 2026-08-20 — see PENTEST-PLAN.md Scenario 2); juiceshop_bruteforce.
common_tools_seen: hydra (unreliable on JSON bodies, see redteam-mcp/README.md)

T1059.001.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell
T1059.001.desc: Use of PowerShell to execute commands/scripts. Note: our own Invoke-WebRequest tooling triggers benign matches.
T1059.001.detection: ET INFO Windows PowerShell User-Agent; PowerShell script-block logging (frequently a false positive here — see below).
T1059.001.false_positive_confirmed: 2026-08-20: a real alert fired on the script block '$global:?' — a harmless built-in PowerShell automatic variable, not attacker code. Judge on script-block CONTENT (obfuscation/download-execute patterns), never the alert title alone.

T1547.001.name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
T1547.001.desc: Persistence via registry Run keys or the Startup folder so code runs at logon.
T1547.001.detection: Sysmon registry-set on Run-key paths; New Service / autostart rules.

T1053.005.name: Scheduled Task/Job: Scheduled Task
T1053.005.desc: Persistence/execution via a Windows scheduled task.
T1053.005.false_positive_confirmed: 2026-08-20: a real alert fired on a genuine Windows Update task (path \Microsoft\Windows\UpdateOrchestrator\...) — pure OS activity, no attacker involved. Check the task PATH against known OS/vendor built-ins before treating as an attack — see agent_kb/playbooks/windows-persistence.md.

T1053.003.name: Scheduled Task/Job: Cron
T1053.003.desc: Persistence/execution on Linux via cron. In this lab the same class as our own @reboot/health-check cron mitigations.
T1053.003.detection: auditd/syslog cron modifications on the Linux host.

T1136.001.name: Create Account: Local Account
T1136.001.desc: Creating a local account for persistent access (the E-7 Windows backdoor account is exactly this).
T1136.001.detection: Security 4720 account creation; net user add.

T1098.name: Account Manipulation
T1098.desc: Modifying an account (group membership, credentials) to maintain access, e.g. adding a user to Administrators.

T1548.name: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism
T1548.desc: Bypassing elevation controls (UAC on Windows, sudo/setuid on Linux) to gain higher privileges.
T1548.detection: Sysmon elevation/UAC-bypass patterns; sudo abuse in auditd.

T1071.001.name: Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
T1071.001.desc: C2 tunneled over HTTP/HTTPS (e.g. Cobalt Strike / AsyncRAT / AdaptixC2 beacons). The C-1 capture and the agent's own verified armed L1 block (202.61.130.163) are this technique.
T1071.001.detection: ET MALWARE C2 beacon signatures; enrichment via VT/AbuseIPDB/GreyNoise/ThreatFox corroboration.
common_tools_seen: real ThreatFox IOCs injected as honestly-tagged synthetic alerts (Cobalt Strike, AsyncRAT, AdaptixC2)

T1078.name: Valid Accounts
T1078.desc: Use of legitimate credentials (e.g. the stolen admin JWT from Juice Shop) to blend in with normal activity.
T1078.detection: Anomalous logins; the SQLi admin-bypass path that yields a valid admin token (confirmed exploitable live, 2026-08-18: real JWT with role=admin obtained via Burp).
